build: Vite + TypeScript. three.js 3D world (src/render3d) under a 2D canvas UI layer (src/scenes). Pure rules in src/core (unit-tested).
how_to_run: npm install && npm run dev  (open http://localhost:5173, ?reset=1 wipes the save, ?seed=N, ?speed=N)
how_to_test: npm test ; npm run build ; npx vite preview --port 4173 & node tools/playtest.mjs --trips 6 --skill 0.7 --shots (playtests run against the preview build; HMR reloads break bot runs on the dev server)
current_objective: Get the CATCH→CRAFT→REVEAL→PROGRESS slice in front of real players and measure the first-session funnel.
biggest_known_problem: Zero real-player evidence. Everything about fun or retention is unvalidated. Second biggest: there is no analytics backend, so even when someone plays we learn nothing.
active_experiment: EXP-001: does the 3D jar reveal plus 'ferments while you fish' drive a second fishing trip? (needs real players)
recent_results: v0 2D slice: bot completes catch → seal → trip → reveal → sell → upgrade with no errors.
Founder asked for cute three.js 3D: the world, fishing, catch trophy and jar reveal are now 3D; UI fish icons are rendered from the 3D models.
[SIM] A skilled bot (0.7) lands 13-15 of 15 casts, mostly perfect; a low-skill bot (0.3) lands 20 of 20 with only 4 perfect. Skill currently drives quality (°N, coins) far more than catch success.
constraints: No real-money gambling, no randomized paid rewards (needs founder/legal approval).
No sensitive personal data. Analytics uses an anonymous random install id only.
Founder approval is needed before spending money (hosting beyond free tiers, paid UA).
next_recommended_action: 1) FOUNDER: enable GitHub Pages and merge this branch to main to get a playable URL; approve an analytics sink. 2) Recruit 5-10 casual playtesters and watch the first 10 minutes. 3) Meanwhile: decide whether catching should carry real failure risk (reef fish harder), add an ambient sound loop, and make the Reef visually distinct (coral, rocks).
